business.title: Field-based estimation of bulk and wall chlorine decay in continuous and intermittent water distribution systems: a study from Coimbatore, India
business.description: Maintaining appropriate residual chlorine in drinking water distribution systems is crucial for ensuring disinfection protection. This study uses field data from two urban distribution zones in Coimbatore, India—Jayaram Nagar, operating under continuous water supply, and Gandhi Park, operating under intermittent water supply to develop a deterministic first-order kinetic-based web framework for estimating bulk and wall chlorine decay coefficients. During the summer of 2024, 96 locations were sampled, comprising 37 in Gandhi Park and 59 in Jayaram Nagar. Bulk ($${k}_{b}$$) and wall ($${k}_{w}$$) decay coefficients were estimated using first-order kinetic equations, with hydraulic contact time approximated from pipe length and flow velocity and empirical adjustments applied for selected water-quality parameters. Across both zones, $${k}_{b}$$ ranged from 0.059 to 0.092 h⁻1 and $${k}_{w}$$ from 0.015 to 0.034 h⁻1. Gandhi Park exhibited mean $${k}_{b}$$ and $${k}_{w}$$ values of 0.078 and 0.026 h⁻1, respectively, compared with 0.076 and 0.025 h⁻1 in Jayaram Nagar. The mean numerical ratio of the estimated bulk to wall decay coefficients was approximately 3:1 in both zones; however, this ratio is reported only as a comparison of coefficient magnitudes and does not represent the actual relative mass contribution of bulk and wall reactions to chlorine loss. However, the differences between the two zones were only 0.002 h⁻1 for $${k}_{b}$$ and 0.001 h⁻1 for $${k}_{w}$$ and were smaller than the corresponding within-zone variability; therefore, the observed differences were interpreted descriptively rather than as statistically established effects of the supply regime. The developed application supports CSV-based and manual data entry and provides transparent sample-level estimates for preliminary engineering assessment.

science.title: Effect of polypropylene fiber length and content on the wet–dry durability of xanthan gum-stabilized clayey sand: mechanical response and ultrasonic monitoring
science.description: Biopolymer soil stabilization offers environmental benefits, but susceptibility to moisture cycling may limit long-term durability. This study assessed the effect of polypropylene (PP) fiber reinforcement on the wetting–drying (W–D) durability of clayey sand stabilized with 0.25% xanthan gum (XG). Specimens containing 0.4% or 0.8% PP fibers, with lengths of 6–12 mm, were cured for 7 days and exposed to up to six W–D cycles. Degradation was evaluated using cumulative mass loss (CML), relative axial height change, unconfined compressive strength (UCS), and ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV), while microstructural changes were examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The XG-stabilized specimen without fibers disintegrated about 1 h after initial immersion, whereas adding 0.8% 6-mm fibers extended specimen integrity beyond 280 h. After six W–D cycles, this specimen exhibited a 7.84% wetting-induced height increase, a 2.2% drying-induced height reduction, a CML of 10.3%, and reductions of 62.5% and 88.9% in UCS and UPV, respectively. SEM images showed that fiber bridging and particle retention delayed disintegration. Overall, selecting an appropriate PP fiber length and content can improve the W–D durability of XG-stabilized soils.

science.title: Crocin alleviates renal fibrosis through inhibiting mitochondrial dysfunction via regulating HOXD8/PGC‑1α pathways
science.description: Crocin, a key bioactive compound derived from saffron (Crocus sativus L.), a traditional Chinese medicinal and edible herb, exhibits renoprotective effects against fibrosis, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that homeobox D8 (HOXD8) and PGC1-α are downregulated, while reactive oxygen species levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and fibrosis are increased in kidney fibrosis models. HOXD8 overexpression increases PGC1-α expression, reduces reactive oxygen species, restores mitochondrial function, and suppresses profibrotic genes. Crocin upregulates HOXD8 and mitigates mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis. Mechanistically, HOXD8 binds the PGC1-α promoter and enhances its transcription. DNMT1-mediated promoter hypermethylation drives HOXD8 downregulation, and crocin reduces DNMT1 enrichment and activity at this promoter. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay support a potential interaction between crocin and HOXD8, and crocin reduces HOXD8 ubiquitination. These findings suggest that crocin upregulates HOXD8 by inhibiting both its promoter hypermethylation and protein ubiquitination, thereby ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis in chronic kidney disease (CKD).
